tweets.text: When working with a new team, how do you “reset” from past professional trauma/dysfunction?

Interesting observation:

OH: “When looking to hire leaders, I look to people who have lead w/o formal authority. Because on some level, it is easier to lead when people report to you. It is easier to appear as if you are visionary and decisive.”

wrapping my head around that.

The sad cycle ...

It happens so predictably. There are a couple points where you can intervene, but it is still hard. https://twitter.com/johncutlefish/status/1208069709574238208/photo/1
What is the least intrusive/least threatening question to ask a prospective employer that will yield the most information about the culture ?

team activity ...

"Describe the role of Manager without using the words Manager or Leader"

the idea that engineer minutes are so incredibly precious -- that they must be micromanaged and hyper-optimized -- is at the root of so much dysfunction.

...premature convergence, Tetris playing, distancing from customers, risk-aversion, efficiency over efficacy, silos

#ux and developer collaboration on a real initiative. What *really* happened. This is why I have trouble answering "so what do you think of dual track?" .

... because teams that are in the zone adapt their approach constantly to match the problem & work

Really love this. 60+ companies represented. 150+ ppl

*Experiments that resulted in increased momentum
*Experiments that "failed", but that taught the team something new
